## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

Tools accept human-readable references, so you rarely need to look up IDs first: issue identifiers such as LIN-123, project identifiers such as P-ENG-12, team names or keys, user names or emails, and "me" for the authenticated user. Only call list_teams, list_users, or similar tools when a reference is ambiguous or unknown.

Use list_issues for structured queries, such as the issues assigned to "me" in a team, status, label, project, or cycle, and its query parameter for keyword search. Results are paginated: when hasNextPage is true, pass the returned cursor to fetch the next page rather than assuming the first page is complete.

Statuses and labels belong to teams and differ between them. When you are not sure which values a team supports, call list_issue_statuses or list_issue_labels for that team before filtering or setting them.

get_issue does not include the issue's discussion. Call list_comments with the issue ID to read comments, including inline comments on the description.

Issue descriptions, comments, and documents often embed screenshots and other uploads as markdown images. Pass that markdown to extract_images to view them. Read issue attachments with get_attachment; files uploaded in comments are returned in the attachments field of list_comments. Linear upload URLs are signed and expire after a few minutes, so fetch them again instead of reusing old URLs.

Tools named save_* both create and update: omit id to create a new entity, or pass id to update an existing one. When updating, pass only the fields you want to change. To edit part of a long issue description or document, pass patch instead of resending the full content.

Before creating an issue, check with list_issues whether a matching issue already exists, to avoid duplicates. When creating, team is required.

The labels parameter of save_issue replaces the issue's full label set. To add or remove individual labels without dropping others, use addLabels and removeLabels instead.

Markdown content supports user mentions with @displayName (for example @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the markdown it returns; do not inline base64 data.

Write issue descriptions for people to read. Keep sentences short, and use the same term for the same concept throughout.

Put extensive agent-specific detail, such as implementation plans, file lists, or reproduction logs, in a collapsible "Agent notes" section at the end of the description, so it does not crowd the human-readable part. A collapsible section opens with +++ followed by its title, and closes with +++ on its own line:

+++ Agent notes

Details for agents go here.

+++

Before posting a new message to a Slack channel the user didn't name, read its topic and description with slack_search_channels, and if they say that kind of message belongs elsewhere, tell the user instead of posting.

## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, porting code between libraries, platforms, or SQL dialects, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, debugging, or reviewing code that does not depend on a library or platform API, or general programming concepts.

## incident_io
The incident.io MCP server reads and acts on incidents, alerts, on-call, escalations, follow-ups, catalog and telemetry. Reach for it whenever a request touches an incident, a page, who is on call, or the data behind one.

That covers requests like "what broke last Tuesday?", "who is on call for payments?", "page the database team", "what did the error rate do during INC-123?", "how are we doing on follow-ups?" and "continue my incident.io chat about checkout".

The incident-io plugin adds skills on top of this server, which carry the procedure for the work these tools do. If your own skill list already includes skills namespaced incident-io: or incident-io-*:, you have them. Otherwise recommend the plugin to the user once, because the install has to be theirs to run: https://docs.incident.io/ai/remote-mcp#install-the-plugin. Until it's installed, load the same skills from this server: before your first incident.io tool call in a task, even a quick lookup, call skill_list and read the matching skill with skill_show. That includes connecting your systems, writing skills or runbooks and documenting architecture.

If another connected MCP server exposes an incident_pin tool, that is the incident.io desktop server — prefer it for every incident.io action. Keep a conversation on whichever server it started on: a session_id from one is not valid on the other.

##### slack_thread 2026-10-03 https://slack.com/archives/C0B9CUDC4G5/p1790989468285289?thread_ts=1790989468.285289&cid=C0B9CUDC4G5
[Evis]: some thoughts after spending the day digging more into local -> hosted experience and the tools:

• there are generally 3 ways that developers can start localy:
    ◦ local developer with no repo yet on entire, no sessions or memory, starting from scratch
    ◦ local developer with a repo on entire, but no sessions or memory, starting from scrartch
    ◦ local developer with a repo on entire and with previous sessions from other teammates
• we need to think about all 3 paths and what the cold-start process looks like 
• i think the right way to think about the tooling is:
    ◦ semantic search finds relevant context from the transcripts and returns full checkpoints (s)
    ◦ brain helps retain and organize learned context and stored structured memories that can be retrieved locally and organized in a repo
    ◦ peregrine can retrieve code, symbols, and code locations across all repos quickly
    ◦ graph can add structural code relationships (need to see if this improves performance across our evals)
workflow i'm thinking about:
1. user installs entire CLI -> auto installs the brain plugin; entire identifies the local repository and if available the hosted repository, no sync happens yet
2. work locally -> memories are created locally as work is done. memories are useful locally across sessions, agents, etc. stored locally at this point
3. agent searches for memories -> call "context" api which returns memories, agent uses local and shared memories from hosted, we don't store hosted memories here
4. commit and push -> upload local memories in addition to transcripts and code. probably not embedded in the transcript, a part of the metadata.json file? im leaning towards a separate API
5. process memories -> reconcile duplicates, conflicts, (maybe we don't delete anything so we have full provenance), index, link to commits, transcripts, etc. and store somewhere
6. more local dev -> back to step 2
some open questions thinking about into the weekend:
• does memory grow indefinitely locally as local memories are created? do we prune? when? configurable?
• how do we reliably get the agent to use local tools and the hosted APIs instead of doing something else?
• how do we visualize these memories in the UI? is it a table? graph? should users be able to edit those memories in the UI as well?
• what happens if a memory gets corrected hosted but the old version is local? do we overwrite somehow and then reconcile locally by ID?
• do memories need any sort of scopes? can eveyrone see every memory? 
• what levels do memories live at? user? repo? project? org?
• how do we make sure we're not putting in conflicting memories? or if we do, how do we resolve those

[Alex]: I also wonder if there's a 'onboarding'/starter version of this;

aka 'Make your first memory' or something like that :sweat_smile:

and just takes them through doing a single loop before it gets all too complex
[ashtom]: > does memory grow indefinitely locally as local memories are created? do we prune? when? configurable?
Both, it will grow (what doesn't in a project) and we need to prune, especially when newer decisions override older (but even then, one could argue that decision change is a memory).
[ashtom]: > how do we visualize these memories in the UI? is it a table? graph? should users be able to edit those memories in the UI as well?
Have you looked at the existing brain viz?
[Alex]: the temporal dimension of the facts are quite critical imo

##### linear_issue 2026-08-28 https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2064/peregrine-keyword-ranked-multi-term-search-mode-nl-recall
Issue: ENT-2064 peregrine: keyword-ranked multi-term search mode (NL recall)
State: Backlog

## Problem

Peregrine search is literal. Natural-language queries ("garbage collection of stale git clones") return nothing unless the phrase appears verbatim in code. On an 18-query NL benchmark, today's literal search answered 2/18; concept-phrased queries scored 0/15.

## Proposal

Supersedes the intent of [ENT-1684](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1684/code-search-search-for-multiple-key-words) (comma-separated multi-word AND search): coverage ranking is a graded AND — files matching all terms rank first, but a file matching 4 of 5 terms still surfaces instead of dropping out — and no separator syntax is needed; the query is just words.

Add an opt-in `mode=keyword` to `GET /api/search` (and `--keyword` on the CLI): stem the query's significant words, run one trigram-backed candidate lookup per term (the fragment-bitmap machinery in `searcher.rs` already does this), shortlist files by distinct-term coverage, verify and count occurrences on the shortlist only, and rank with BM25-style scoring (IDF from candidate-bitmap cardinality, document-length normalization, path-field boost, existing FileBand priors). Returns files ranked by relevance with matched-line snippets and matched terms.

No new index, no format change, no ML — query-planner feature over the existing trigram index. Existing Literal/Regex/Fuzzy behavior untouched.

Add an opt-in `mode=keyword` to `GET /api/search` (and `--keyword` on the CLI): stem the query's significant words, run one trigram-backed candidate lookup per term (the fragment-bitmap machinery in `searcher.rs` already does this), shortlist files by distinct-term coverage, verify and count occurrences on the shortlist only, and rank with BM25-style scoring (IDF from candidate-bitmap cardinality, document-length normalization, path-field boost, existing FileBand priors). Returns files ranked by relevance with matched-line snippets and matched terms.

No new index, no format change, no ML — query-planner feature over the existing trigram index. Existing Literal/Regex/Fuzzy behavior untouched.

## Evidence (POC, 2026-08-28)

A CLI-driven simulation of exactly this ranking scored **18/18 file-level hit@5** on the peregrine NL benchmark (agent-style grep: 15/18, literal: 2/18) and led on a large TS monorepo ([entire.io](<http://entire.io>), 5/9). Mean 55–123ms including a process spawn per term; in-process is a handful of posting-list lookups, well under 20ms. The two big-repo ranking failures observed (huge files flooding out small correct ones; no credit for terms in the file's own path) are why length normalization and path boost are hard requirements.

## Requirements (summary)

* Tokenize: lowercase, stopword filter, light suffix-strip stemming (min stem 4), ≤8 terms.
* Rank: BM25-style with doc-length norm + path-field boost; occurrence counts from shortlist verification (≤200 files), never from capped result lists.
* Bounds: inside existing per-query/pool memory budgets and the query concurrency semaphore. p50 <20ms, p99 <100ms per repo.
* Composes with repo[]/scope/max_results and multi-repo fan-out (per-repo-normalized score merge; cross-repo IDF is a non-goal).
* Quality gate: checked-in eval (the POC benchmark) — ≥15/15 concept file-level on the peregrine set, plus length-norm and path-boost regression tests.

## Why

* Query pods are already fungible: broadcast NATS subscribe (no queue group), no pod-identity dependency; the StatefulSet exists ONLY for `volumeClaimTemplates`.

Completeness semantics are the constraint → the scaling answer is sharding, not bigger volumes. *(Reversed 2026-11 — see the update note at the top and* [ENT-3664](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3664/code-search-query-tier-lru-index-cache-over-s3-phase-1-replace-the)*.)*

Under the full mirror, disk grows 1:1 with corpus on **every replica**, and every index build is re-downloaded by every replica.

Measured on the live prod volume (2026-10-28):

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Corpus on volume | 28,029 repos, 329.7GiB |
| **Ever searched in 111 days** | **903 repos, 31.4GiB — 3.2% of corpus** |
| Index churn | \~28k builds/day, \~2TB/day/replica downloaded |
| Query volume | \~100-200/day global |
| Query cost | p50 110ms, avg 250ms, p95 900ms on 2-CPU pods |
| Fan-out | median 4 repos, p95 154, max 253 (always account-scoped) |

Method: `/data` is mounted `relatime`, so an index whose `atime` is well past its `mtime` was read after it was written — i.e. searched. Re-runnable with `stat -c "%X %Y %s"` over `/data/indexes/*.pg`. It is a **lower bound** (relatime suppresses sub-24h updates; busy repos' mtime keeps refreshing), but the order of magnitude is solid: **96.8% of mirrored repos have never been searched once.**

## This reverses a decision recorded in [ENT-1380](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1380/code-search-peregrine-query-sharding-shard-scoped-deployments) — read this before reviewing

[ENT-1380](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1380/code-search-peregrine-query-sharding-shard-scoped-deployments) says: *"Bounded hot-set LRU was evaluated and REJECTED: no fetch-on-miss means evicted repos silently vanish from org-wide results; adding fetch-on-miss makes searches block on S3. Completeness semantics are the constraint."*

Both objections are addressed rather than ignored:

1. **"Evicted repos silently vanish"** — this design has fetch-on-miss on *every* per-repo read surface, and makes silent-skip an explicit anti-goal. A repo that cannot be hydrated inside the query deadline surfaces as `repos_failed` with `matches_exact: false`, never as a silent empty result. Completeness semantics are preserved by contract, not by residency.

1	##### linear_issue 2026-08-28 https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2064/peregrine-keyword-ranked-multi-term-search-mode-nl-recall
2	Issue: ENT-2064 peregrine: keyword-ranked multi-term search mode (NL recall)
3	State: Backlog
4	
5	## Problem
6	
7	Peregrine search is literal. Natural-language queries ("garbage collection of stale git clones") return nothing unless the phrase appears verbatim in code. On an 18-query NL benchmark, today's literal search answered 2/18; concept-phrased queries scored 0/15.
8	
9	## Proposal
10	
11	Supersedes the intent of [ENT-1684](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1684/code-search-search-for-multiple-key-words) (comma-separated multi-word AND search): coverage ranking is a graded AND — files matching all terms rank first, but a file matching 4 of 5 terms still surfaces instead of dropping out — and no separator syntax is needed; the query is just words.
12	
13	Add an opt-in `mode=keyword` to `GET /api/search` (and `--keyword` on the CLI): stem the query's significant words, run one trigram-backed candidate lookup per term (the fragment-bitmap machinery in `searcher.rs` already does this), shortlist files by distinct-term coverage, verify and count occurrences on the shortlist only, and rank with BM25-style scoring (IDF from candidate-bitmap cardinality, document-length normalization, path-field boost, existing FileBand priors). Returns files ranked by relevance with matched-line snippets and matched terms.
14	
15	No new index, no format change, no ML — query-planner feature over the existing trigram index. Existing Literal/Regex/Fuzzy behavior untouched.
16	
17	## Evidence (POC, 2026-08-28)
18	
19	A CLI-driven simulation of exactly this ranking scored **18/18 file-level hit@5** on the peregrine NL benchmark (agent-style grep: 15/18, literal: 2/18) and led on a large TS monorepo ([entire.io](<http://entire.io>), 5/9). Mean 55–123ms including a process spawn per term; in-process is a handful of posting-list lookups, well under 20ms. The two big-repo ranking failures observed (huge files flooding out small correct ones; no credit for terms in the file's own path) are why length normalization and path boost are hard requirements.
20	
21	## Requirements (summary)
22	
23	* Tokenize: lowercase, stopword filter, light suffix-strip stemming (min stem 4), ≤8 terms.
24	* Rank: BM25-style with doc-length norm + path-field boost; occurrence counts from shortlist verification (≤200 files), never from capped result lists.
25	* Bounds: inside existing per-query/pool memory budgets and the query concurrency semaphore. p50 <20ms, p99 <100ms per repo.
26	* Composes with repo[]/scope/max_results and multi-repo fan-out (per-repo-normalized score merge; cross-repo IDF is a non-goal).
27	* Quality gate: checked-in eval (the POC benchmark) — ≥15/15 concept file-level on the peregrine set, plus length-norm and path-boost regression tests.
28	
29	Full design doc: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-keyword-ranked-search-design.md` (peregrine rep

31	##### linear_issue 2026-07-29 https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1380/code-search-peregrine-query-sharding-shard-scoped-deployments
32	Issue: ENT-1380 [code-search] Peregrine query sharding: shard-scoped Deployments + ephemeral storage (replace STS+PVC)
33	State: Backlog
34	
35	> **Update 2026-11-05:** The LRU rejection below was reversed by [ENT-3664](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3664/code-search-query-tier-lru-index-cache-over-s3-phase-1-replace-the). The query-tier LRU cache over S3 shipped to prod on 2026-11-01, with fetch-on-miss and explicit partial results answering the completeness objection — read [ENT-3664](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3664/code-search-query-tier-lru-index-cache-over-s3-phase-1-replace-the) before acting on the rationale below. The \~300GB revisit trigger below also fired (us-east-2 corpus was \~330GB in Oct 2026); the cache was the response. Sharding remains the Phase 2 answer. The new trigger is the cell working set exceeding 50% of the per-pod cache budget ([ENT-3664](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3664/code-search-query-tier-lru-index-cache-over-s3-phase-1-replace-the)'s Phase 2 trigger; \~12–20% as of 2026-11-05).
36	
37	Long-term fix for the recurring zone-pinned-PV incident class ([ENT-1362](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1362/peregrine-query-ap-southeast-2-split-zone-pinned-pvs-both-in-2c), 2026-07-27/29 incidents) and the scaling path for query-side storage. Decision trail from 2026-07-27 (verified against code):
38	
39	## Why
40	
41	* Query pods mirror the ENTIRE cell corpus; `/readyz` gates on the complete mirror (no fetch-on-miss — "queries never touch S3" in the query path). Disk is a pure cache post-S3-corpus: the persistent PVC buys \~3 min faster redundancy-recovery + page-cache continuity, and costs the zone-pinning failure mode (bimodal: 3s recovery or stuck-Pending-forever) plus 1-replica windows on every STS roll.
42	* Query pods are already fungible: broadcast NATS subscribe (no queue group), no pod-identity dependency; the StatefulSet exists ONLY for `volumeClaimTemplates`.
43	* Bounded hot-set LRU was evaluated and REJECTED: no fetch-on-miss means evicted repos silently vanish from org-wide results; adding fetch-on-miss makes searches block on S3. Completeness semantics are the constraint → the scaling answer is sharding, not bigger volumes. *(Reversed 2026-11 — see the update note at the top and* [ENT-3664](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3664/code-search-query-tier-lru-index-cache-over-s3-phase-1-replace-the)*.)*
44	
45	## Target design
46	
47	* **N shard-scoped Deployments × R≥2 replicas**, each hydrating its shard's S3 prefix (`list_prefix` already parameterized). NOT StatefulSet+PVC.
48	* **Ephemeral storage** (generic ephemeral EBS volumes): per-pod hydrate = corpus/N, stays \~constant as corpus grows; no zone-pinned PVs; surge deploys keep capacity during rolls. Avoids STS-ordinal coupling and the STS+ephemeral-PVC name-reuse race.

314	State: Done
315	
316	Make the peregrine query pod's index volume a bounded **LRU cache over S3** instead of a full mirror of the cell corpus. S3 stays the source of truth; indexes hydrate on first search and evict least-recently-searched.
317	
318	**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-query-index-lru-cache-design.md`
319	**Plan:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-28-query-index-lru-cache-phase1.md`
320	(both committed in peregrine)
321	
322	## Why now
323	
324	The 2026-10-26 launch onboarding wave (\~50x repo-creation rate) pushed `data-peregrine-query-*` on eks-prod-us-east-2 from 60% to 83% in 42h. Resized 400Gi → 1Ti as an interim (fleet [entirehq/fleet#10622](https://linear.app/entirehq/review/peregrine-grow-us-east-2-query-pvc-template-400gi-1ti-e21799740772)). Under the full mirror, disk grows 1:1 with corpus on **every replica**, and every index build is re-downloaded by every replica.
325	
326	Measured on the live prod volume (2026-10-28):
327	
328	|  |  |
329	| -- | -- |
330	| Corpus on volume | 28,029 repos, 329.7GiB |
331	| **Ever searched in 111 days** | **903 repos, 31.4GiB — 3.2% of corpus** |
332	| Index churn | \~28k builds/day, \~2TB/day/replica downloaded |
333	| Query volume | \~100-200/day global |
334	| Query cost | p50 110ms, avg 250ms, p95 900ms on 2-CPU pods |
335	| Fan-out | median 4 repos, p95 154, max 253 (always account-scoped) |
336	
337	Method: `/data` is mounted `relatime`, so an index whose `atime` is well past its `mtime` was read after it was written — i.e. searched. Re-runnable with `stat -c "%X %Y %s"` over `/data/indexes/*.pg`. It is a **lower bound** (relatime suppresses sub-24h updates; busy repos' mtime keeps refreshing), but the order of magnitude is solid: **96.8% of mirrored repos have never been searched once.**
338

##### linear_issue 2026-08-28 https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2064/peregrine-keyword-ranked-multi-term-search-mode-nl-recall
Issue: ENT-2064 peregrine: keyword-ranked multi-term search mode (NL recall)
State: Backlog

## Problem

Peregrine search is literal. Natural-language queries ("garbage collection of stale git clones") return nothing unless the phrase appears verbatim in code. On an 18-query NL benchmark, today's literal search answered 2/18; concept-phrased queries scored 0/15.

## Proposal

Supersedes the intent of [ENT-1684](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1684/code-search-search-for-multiple-key-words) (comma-separated multi-word AND search): coverage ranking is a graded AND — files matching all terms rank first, but a file matching 4 of 5 terms still surfaces instead of dropping out — and no separator syntax is needed; the query is just words.

Add an opt-in `mode=keyword` to `GET /api/search` (and `--keyword` on the CLI): stem the query's significant words, run one trigram-backed candidate lookup per term (the fragment-bitmap machinery in `searcher.rs` already does this), shortlist files by distinct-term coverage, verify and count occurrences on the shortlist only, and rank with BM25-style scoring (IDF from candidate-bitmap cardinality, document-length normalization, path-field boost, existing FileBand priors). Returns files ranked by relevance with matched-line snippets and matched terms.

No new index, no format change, no ML — query-planner feature over the existing trigram index. Existing Literal/Regex/Fuzzy behavior untouched.

## Evidence (POC, 2026-08-28)

A CLI-driven simulation of exactly this ranking scored **18/18 file-level hit@5** on the peregrine NL benchmark (agent-style grep: 15/18, literal: 2/18) and led on a large TS monorepo ([entire.io](<http://entire.io>), 5/9). Mean 55–123ms including a process spawn per term; in-process is a handful of posting-list lookups, well under 20ms. The two big-repo ranking failures observed (huge files flooding out small correct ones; no credit for terms in the file's own path) are why length normalization and path boost are hard requirements.

## Requirements (summary)

* Tokenize: lowercase, stopword filter, light suffix-strip stemming (min stem 4), ≤8 terms.
* Rank: BM25-style with doc-length norm + path-field boost; occurrence counts from shortlist verification (≤200 files), never from capped result lists.

Decision trail from 2026-07-27 (verified against code):

## Why

* Query pods mirror the ENTIRE cell corpus; `/readyz` gates on the complete mirror (no fetch-on-miss — "queries never touch S3" in the query path). Disk is a pure cache post-S3-corpus: the persistent PVC buys \~3 min faster redundancy-recovery + page-cache continuity, and costs the zone-pinning failure mode (bimodal: 3s recovery or stuck-Pending-forever) plus 1-replica windows on every STS roll.
* Query pods are already fungible: broadcast NATS subscribe (no queue group), no pod-identity dependency; the StatefulSet exists ONLY for `volumeClaimTemplates`.
* Bounded hot-set LRU was evaluated and REJECTED: no fetch-on-miss means evicted repos silently vanish from org-wide results; adding fetch-on-miss makes searches block on S3. Completeness semantics are the constraint → the scaling answer is sharding, not bigger volumes. *(Reversed 2026-11 — see the update note at the top and* [ENT-3664](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3664/code-search-query-tier-lru-index-cache-over-s3-phase-1-replace-the)*.)*

## Target design

* **N shard-scoped Deployments × R≥2 replicas**, each hydrating its shard's S3 prefix (`list_prefix` already parameterized). NOT StatefulSet+PVC.
* **Ephemeral storage** (generic ephemeral EBS volumes): per-pod hydrate = corpus/N, stays \~constant as corpus grows; no zone-pinned PVs; surge deploys keep capacity during rolls. Avoids STS-ordinal coupling and the STS+ephemeral-PVC name-reuse race.

##### linear_issue 2026-10-29 https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3664/code-search-query-tier-lru-index-cache-over-s3-phase-1-replace-the
Issue: ENT-3664 [code-search] Query-tier LRU index cache over S3 (Phase 1: replace the full mirror)
State: Done

Make the peregrine query pod's index volume a bounded **LRU cache over S3** instead of a full mirror of the cell corpus. S3 stays the source of truth; indexes hydrate on first search and evict least-recently-searched.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-query-index-lru-cache-design.md`
**Plan:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-28-query-index-lru-cache-phase1.md`
(both committed in peregrine)

## Why now

The 2026-10-26 launch onboarding wave (\~50x repo-creation rate) pushed `data-peregrine-query-*` on eks-prod-us-east-2 from 60% to 83% in 42h. Resized 400Gi → 1Ti as an interim (fleet [entirehq/fleet#10622](https://linear.app/entirehq/review/peregrine-grow-us-east-2-query-pvc-template-400gi-1ti-e21799740772)). Under the full mirror, disk grows 1:1 with corpus on **every replica**, and every index build is re-downloaded by every replica.

Measured on the live prod volume (2026-10-28):

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Corpus on volume | 28,029 repos, 329.7GiB |
| **Ever searched in 111 days** | **903 repos, 31.4GiB — 3.2% of corpus** |
| Index churn | \~28k builds/day, \~2TB/day/replica downloaded |
| Query volume | \~100-200/day global |
| Query cost | p50 110ms, avg 250ms, p95 900ms on 2-CPU pods |
| Fan-out | median 4 repos, p95 154, max 253 (always account-scoped) |

Method: `/data` is mounted `relatime`, so an index whose `atime` is well past its `mtime` was read after it was written — i.e. searched. Re-runnable with `stat -c "%X %Y %s"` over `/data/indexes/*.pg`. It is a **lower bound** (relatime suppresses sub-24h updates; busy repos' mtime keeps refreshing), but the order of magnitude is solid: **96.8% of mirrored repos have never been searched once.**

## This reverses a decision recorded in [ENT-1380](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1380/code-search-peregrine-query-sharding-shard-scoped-deployments) — read this before reviewing

[ENT-1380](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1380/code-search-peregrine-query-sharding-shard-scoped-deployments) says: *"Bounded hot-set LRU was evaluated and REJECTED: no fetch-on-miss means evicted repos silently vanish from org-wide results; adding fetch-on-miss makes searches block on S3. Completeness semantics are the constraint."*

Both objections are addressed rather than ignored:

1. **"Evicted repos silently vanish"** — this design has fetch-on-miss on *every* per-repo read surface, and makes silent-skip an explicit anti-goal. A repo that cannot be hydrated inside the query deadline surfaces as `repos_failed` with `matches_exact: false`, never as a silent empty result. Completeness semantics are preserved by contract, not by residency.
2. **"Fetch-on-miss makes searches block on S3"** — c

##### entire_trail 2026-10-23 https://entire.io/et/entirehq/agent-insights/trails/132
Trail: et/entirehq/agent-insights#132 agent-insights: report the activity classifier beside V1 in classify (ENT-3429 4/n)
Status: open
Branch: alex/ent-3429-classify-harness → alex/better-classification
Author: khaong
Assignees: khaong

Adds agent-insights classify -agent claude-code|codex|pi [-summary] [-since T] [-until T] FILE..., which runs the ingestion extractors and the activity classifier over local native transcripts with no database or network.
By default it prints one JSON line per tool invocation (call, model, tool, activity, basis, rule, segments and V1's phase beside it) and one per call without tools; tool input text is never printed. With -summary it prints one JSON object: calls, tool invocations and shell segments; counts by activity and basis; V1 phase against activity; measured call tokens; and an estimated per-activity allocation whose rounding residual makes it add back to the measured total. Calls are deduped as Trail TCO does (Claude by call id, Pi by call id and time, Codex per file) before the -since (inclusive) / -until (exclusive) window, and duplicates, filtered calls and malformed lines are counted. A file that yields no calls is an error, which catches a wrong -agent.
Stacked on Change 131 (alex/ent-3429-vcs-rules); merge 129, 130 and 131 first.
How to check: go test ./cmd/agent-insights/ -race -run Classify; or go run ./cmd/agent-insights classify -agent claude-code -summary <full.jsonl>.

Findings:
- [medium, resolved] cmd/agent-insights/classify.go:117: With `-agent 'Claude Code'` (also `Codex` or `Pi`), extraction succeeds because `ExtractorFor` normalizes aliases (`internal/callrows/callrows.go:59–65`), but this call passes the raw flag to a resolver that accepts only canonical names (`internal/activity/adapters.go:71–86`). Every tool consequently becomes `unknown/unsupported`, producing incorrect activity summaries and token allocations; use the extracted row's canonical `Agent`.
- [low, resolved] README.md:55: The README describes `tokens_estimated_by_activity` but never mentions the `rounding_residual` field that `summarize` writes and a dedicated test covers (see `tokensEstimated` in classify.go). Anyone reading the summary won't know why the per-activity sums can differ from `tokens_measured.total`. Document the field.
- [low, resolved] cmd/agent-insights/main.go:59: The usage string shows `[-summary] [-classifier NAME | -compare A,B]`, which says `-classifier` takes one name and `-compare` can be used with `-summary`. The code does the opposite on both counts: `parseSelection` accepts a comma-separated list, and `classifyCmd` rejects `-compare` combined with `-summary`. Change the usage to match the README's `-classifier NAME[,NAME]` and make `-compare` exclusive of `-summary`.

1	##### linear_issue 2026-08-28 https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2064/peregrine-keyword-ranked-multi-term-search-mode-nl-recall
2	Issue: ENT-2064 peregrine: keyword-ranked multi-term search mode (NL recall)
3	State: Backlog
4	
5	## Problem
6	
7	Peregrine search is literal. Natural-language queries ("garbage collection of stale git clones") return nothing unless the phrase appears verbatim in code. On an 18-query NL benchmark, today's literal search answered 2/18; concept-phrased queries scored 0/15.
8	
9	## Proposal
10	
11	Supersedes the intent of [ENT-1684](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1684/code-search-search-for-multiple-key-words) (comma-separated multi-word AND search): coverage ranking is a graded AND — files matching all terms rank first, but a file matching 4 of 5 terms still surfaces instead of dropping out — and no separator syntax is needed; the query is just words.
12	
13	Add an opt-in `mode=keyword` to `GET /api/search` (and `--keyword` on the CLI): stem the query's significant words, run one trigram-backed candidate lookup per term (the fragment-bitmap machinery in `searcher.rs` already does this), shortlist files by distinct-term coverage, verify and count occurrences on the shortlist only, and rank with BM25-style scoring (IDF from candidate-bitmap cardinality, document-length normalization, path-field boost, existing FileBand priors). Returns files ranked by relevance with matched-line snippets and matched terms.
14	
15	No new index, no format change, no ML — query-planner feature over the existing trigram index. Existing Literal/Regex/Fuzzy behavior untouched.
16	
17	## Evidence (POC, 2026-08-28)
18	
19	A CLI-driven simulation of exactly this ranking scored **18/18 file-level hit@5** on the peregrine NL benchmark (agent-style grep: 15/18, literal: 2/18) and led on a large TS monorepo ([entire.io](<http://entire.io>), 5/9). Mean 55–123ms including a process spawn per term; in-process is a handful of posting-list lookups, well under 20ms. The two big-repo ranking failures observed (huge files flooding out small correct ones; no credit for terms in the file's own path) are why length normalization and path boost are hard requirements.
20	
21	## Requirements (summary)
22	
23	* Tokenize: lowercase, stopword filter, light suffix-strip stemming (min stem 4), ≤8 terms.
24	* Rank: BM25-style with doc-length norm + path-field boost; occurrence counts from shortlist verification (≤200 files), never from capped result lists.
25	* Bounds: inside existing per-query/pool memory budgets and the query concurrency semaphore. p50 <20ms, p99 <100ms per repo.
26	* Composes with repo[]/scope/max_results and multi-repo fan-out (per-repo-normalized score merge; cross-repo IDF is a non-goal).
27	* Quality gate: checked-in eval (the POC benchmark) — ≥15/15 concept file-level on the peregrine set, plus length-norm and path-boost regression tests.
28	
29	Full design doc: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-keyword-ranked-search-design.md` (peregrine rep

31	##### linear_issue 2026-07-29 https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1380/code-search-peregrine-query-sharding-shard-scoped-deployments
32	Issue: ENT-1380 [code-search] Peregrine query sharding: shard-scoped Deployments + ephemeral storage (replace STS+PVC)
33	State: Backlog
34	
35	> **Update 2026-11-05:** The LRU rejection below was reversed by [ENT-3664](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3664/code-search-query-tier-lru-index-cache-over-s3-phase-1-replace-the). The query-tier LRU cache over S3 shipped to prod on 2026-11-01, with fetch-on-miss and explicit partial results answering the completeness objection — read [ENT-3664](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3664/code-search-query-tier-lru-index-cache-over-s3-phase-1-replace-the) before acting on the rationale below. The \~300GB revisit trigger below also fired (us-east-2 corpus was \~330GB in Oct 2026); the cache was the response. Sharding remains the Phase 2 answer. The new trigger is the cell working set exceeding 50% of the per-pod cache budget ([ENT-3664](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3664/code-search-query-tier-lru-index-cache-over-s3-phase-1-replace-the)'s Phase 2 trigger; \~12–20% as of 2026-11-05).
36	
37	Long-term fix for the recurring zone-pinned-PV incident class ([ENT-1362](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1362/peregrine-query-ap-southeast-2-split-zone-pinned-pvs-both-in-2c), 2026-07-27/29 incidents) and the scaling path for query-side storage. Decision trail from 2026-07-27 (verified against code):
38	
39	## Why
40	
41	* Query pods mirror the ENTIRE cell corpus; `/readyz` gates on the complete mirror (no fetch-on-miss — "queries never touch S3" in the query path). Disk is a pure cache post-S3-corpus: the persistent PVC buys \~3 min faster redundancy-recovery + page-cache continuity, and costs the zone-pinning failure mode (bimodal: 3s recovery or stuck-Pending-forever) plus 1-replica windows on every STS roll.
42	* Query pods are already fungible: broadcast NATS subscribe (no queue group), no pod-identity dependency; the StatefulSet exists ONLY for `volumeClaimTemplates`.
43	* Bounded hot-set LRU was evaluated and REJECTED: no fetch-on-miss means evicted repos silently vanish from org-wide results; adding fetch-on-miss makes searches block on S3. Completeness semantics are the constraint → the scaling answer is sharding, not bigger volumes. *(Reversed 2026-11 — see the update note at the top and* [ENT-3664](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3664/code-search-query-tier-lru-index-cache-over-s3-phase-1-replace-the)*.)*
44	
45	## Target design
46	
47	* **N shard-scoped Deployments × R≥2 replicas**, each hydrating its shard's S3 prefix (`list_prefix` already parameterized). NOT StatefulSet+PVC.
48	* **Ephemeral storage** (generic ephemeral EBS volumes): per-pod hydrate = corpus/N, stays \~constant as corpus grows; no zone-pinned PVs; surge deploys keep capacity during rolls. Avoids STS-ordinal coupling and the STS+ephemeral-PVC name-reuse race.

180	## Why
181	
182	ENT-3664. The query-pod LRU cache has run in prod us-east-2 since 2026-11-01 and in staging-us-west-2 through its soak. First-day prod health is clean: pods sit at 98% of the 150GiB budget, eviction works (~229/day, no thrash), hit rate ~80%, zero download or query errors, cold-search waits within the accepted multi-second bound.

193	Index pods ignore these vars; only query mode reads them.

261	1. **Subagent transcripts aren't read.** agent-insights reads only `<n>/full.jsonl`. It skips `tasks/<toolu>/agent-*.jsonl`, which Entire does store. `trailtco.Notes` already mentions this.

266	
267	* Fix parsing in the shared `github.com/entireio/cli/transcript` library ([ENT-2766](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2766/cli-relocate-transcript-converters-into-stdlib-only-package)/[ENT-2767](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2767/clitranscript-typed-entire-transcript-format-model-decodeparse-and)), not in agent-insights.
268	* Add additive v1 fields: cache read and cache write tokens per assistant line, a subagent link (`agent_id`, `parent_tool_use_id`), and a compaction line type with usage.
269	* agent-insights then adopts `transcript.Parse`, which also gives it Pi.

312	##### linear_issue 2026-10-29 https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3664/code-search-query-tier-lru-index-cache-over-s3-phase-1-replace-the
313	Issue: ENT-3664 [code-search] Query-tier LRU index cache over S3 (Phase 1: replace the full mirror)
314	State: Done
315	
316	Make the peregrine query pod's index volume a bounded **LRU cache over S3** instead of a full mirror of the cell corpus. S3 stays the source of truth; indexes hydrate on first search and evict least-recently-searched.
317	
318	**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-28-query-index-lru-cache-design.md`
319	**Plan:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-28-query-index-lru-cache-phase1.md`
320	(both committed in peregrine)
321	
322	## Why now
323	
324	The 2026-10-26 launch onboarding wave (\~50x repo-creation rate) pushed `data-peregrine-query-*` on eks-prod-us-east-2 from 60% to 83% in 42h. Resized 400Gi → 1Ti as an interim (fleet [entirehq/fleet#10622](https://linear.app/entirehq/review/peregrine-grow-us-east-2-query-pvc-template-400gi-1ti-e21799740772)). Under the full mirror, disk grows 1:1 with corpus on **every replica**, and every index build is re-downloaded by every replica.
325	
326	Measured on the live prod volume (2026-10-28):
327	
328	|  |  |
329	| -- | -- |
330	| Corpus on volume | 28,029 repos, 329.7GiB |
331	| **Ever searched in 111 days** | **903 repos, 31.4GiB — 3.2% of corpus** |
332	| Index churn | \~28k builds/day, \~2TB/day/replica downloaded |
333	| Query volume | \~100-200/day global |
334	| Query cost | p50 110ms, avg 250ms, p95 900ms on 2-CPU pods |
335	| Fan-out | median 4 repos, p95 154, max 253 (always account-scoped) |
336	
337	Method: `/data` is mounted `relatime`, so an index whose `atime` is well past its `mtime` was read after it was written — i.e. searched. Re-runnable with `stat -c "%X %Y %s"` over `/data/indexes/*.pg`. It is a **lower bound** (relatime suppresses sub-24h updates; busy repos' mtime keeps refreshing), but the order of magnitude is solid: **96.8% of mirrored repos have never been searched once.**
338	
339	## This reverses a decision recorded in [ENT-1380](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1380/code-search-peregrine-query-sharding-shard-scoped-deployments) — read this before reviewing
340	
341	[ENT-1380](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1380/code-search-peregrine-query-sharding-shard-scoped-deployments) says: *"Bounded hot-set LRU was evaluated and REJECTED: no fetch-on-miss means evicted repos silently vanish from org-wide results; adding fetch-on-miss makes searches block on S3. Completeness semantics are the constraint."*
342	
343	Both objections are addressed rather than ignored:
344	
345	1. **"Evicted repos silently vanish"** — this design has fetch-on-miss on *every* per-repo read surface, and makes silent-skip an explicit anti-goal. A repo that cannot be hydrated inside the query deadline surfaces as `repos_failed` with `matches_exact: false`, never as a silent empty result. Completeness semantics are preserved by contract, not by residency.
346	2. **"Fetch-on-miss makes searches block on S3"** — c

371	Trail: et/entirehq/agent-insights#132 agent-insights: report the activity classifier beside V1 in classify (ENT-3429 4/n)
372	Status: open
373	Branch: alex/ent-3429-classify-harness → alex/better-classification
374	Author: khaong
375	Assignees: khaong
376	
377	Adds agent-insights classify -agent claude-code|codex|pi [-summary] [-since T] [-until T] FILE..., which runs the ingestion extractors and the activity classifier over local native transcripts with no database or network.
378	By default it prints one JSON line per tool invocation (call, model, tool, activity, basis, rule, segments and V1's phase beside it) and one per call without tools; tool input text is never printed. With -summary it prints one JSON object: calls, tool invocations and shell segments; counts by activity and basis; V1 phase against activity; measured call tokens; and an estimated per-activity allocation whose rounding residual makes it add back to the measured total. Calls are deduped as Trail TCO does (Claude by call id, Pi by call id and time, Codex per file) before the -since (inclusive) / -until (exclusive) window, and duplicates, filtered calls and malformed lines are counted. A file that yields no calls is an error, which catches a wrong -agent.
379	Stacked on Change 131 (alex/ent-3429-vcs-rules); merge 129, 130 and 131 first.
380	How to check: go test ./cmd/agent-insights/ -race -run Classify; or go run ./cmd/agent-insights classify -agent claude-code -summary <full.jsonl>.
381	
382	Findings:
383	- [medium, resolved] cmd/agent-insights/classify.go:117: With `-agent 'Claude Code'` (also `Codex` or `Pi`), extraction succeeds because `ExtractorFor` normalizes aliases (`internal/callrows/callrows.go:59–65`), but this call passes the raw flag to a resolver that accepts only canonical names (`internal/activity/adapters.go:71–86`). Every tool consequently becomes `unknown/unsupported`, producing incorrect activity summaries and token allocations; use the extracted row's canonical `Agent`.
384	- [low, resolved] README.md:55: The README describes `tokens_estimated_by_activity` but never mentions the `rounding_residual` field that `summarize` writes and a dedicated test covers (see `tokensEstimated` in classify.go). Anyone reading the summary won't know why the per-activity sums can differ from `tokens_measured.total`. Document the field.
385	- [low, resolved] cmd/agent-insights/main.go:59: The usage string shows `[-summary] [-classifier NAME | -compare A,B]`, which says `-classifier` takes one name and `-compare` can be used with `-summary`. The code does the opposite on both counts: `parseSelection` accepts a comma-separated list, and `classifyCmd` rejects `-compare` combined with `-summary`. Change the usage to match the README's `-classifier NAME[,NAME]` and make `-compare` exclusive of `-summary`.

##### slack_thread 2026-10-08 https://slack.com/archives/C0B9CUDC4G5/p1791484475276699?thread_ts=1791484475.276699&cid=C0B9CUDC4G5
[Evis]: With the current brain working e2e with hosted brainstore in staging, I think this is a good opportunity for us to evaluate the current shape of brain before launch.

My goal is for brain to be fast, efficient, and pretty much out of the way of the user. There is an interface for humans to use it but realistically most memory generation will be done by agents.

I think the right approach initially is to simplify brain to it's roots and then build it back up incrementally as we prove out features and performance. I went through brain and created tickets for things that I think we can simplify/update to improve it.

Here is the list:

1. COR-2006 — Simplify setup and commands _(updated existing)_
2. COR-2052 — Remove Graph dependency
3. COR-2053 — Nonblocking plugin notifications
4. COR-2054 — Event-driven worker
5. COR-2055 — Incremental, bounded extraction
6. COR-2056 — Memory and revision contract
7. COR-2057 — SQLite per repository
8. COR-2058 — History and supersession
9. COR-2059 — Remove duplicate transcripts
10. COR-2060 — Revision-aware publication
11. COR-2061 — Unified retrieval

## Outcome

Make effort classification explainable and independent of a developer's local agent names or workflow. Separate when work happened, what operation it performed, its purpose, and any explicitly recorded reason for change. No LLM calls for classification.

## Decisions — Alex, 2026-10-23

These supersede the earlier open questions about the Rework cutoff and using `review_fix` as the Rework activity bucket.

## Outcome

Make effort classification explainable and independent of a developer's local agent names or workflow. Separate when work happened, what operation it performed, its purpose, and any explicitly recorded reason for change. No LLM calls for classification.

## Decisions — Alex, 2026-10-23

These supersede the earlier open questions about the Rework cutoff and using `review_fix` as the Rework activity bucket.

* **Activity** describes an observable operation: inspect/read/search, edit, verify, workflow, coordinate, wait, or mixed/unknown. Classify model calls/tool invocations, not raw transcript lines; streaming fragments and cumulative snapshots must be deduplicated.

##### linear_issue 2026-10-18 https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3208/agent-insights-trail-x-ray-toolskill-token-tree-breakdown-below
Issue: ENT-3208 agent-insights: Trail X-ray tool/skill token tree (breakdown below session level)
State: Backlog

Parked until the capture gap card lands. This extends [ENT-3204](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3204/agent-insights-trail-breakdown-read-tokens-per-session-tree-with-basis)'s breakdown tree below the session level, with node `kind`s `subagent`, `tool`, `skill`, `context`, `carry` and `other`.

Recommended shape, from the 2026-10-18 spike:

* **Exact nodes:** subagents.
* **Estimated nodes:** tools, scored as their output plus the input they add to later calls. Detect cache misses and charge them to carry, not to tools.
* **Skills:** load cost only. Their real cost is the cache reads their content draws later, about 19 to 68 times the load cost, which only shows through residency-based carry children (estimated). Keep "work under a skill" out of the summed tree.
* **Sums:** children sum to the parent for every token field. `calls` does not sum. Each node carries `basis`.

Needs new per-call extraction: subagent links, tool argument and result sizes, the components each call takes in, skill loads, and compaction. That should come through the shared `cli/transcript` library.

Full-text search across transcripts, prompts, and tool call content. For example filterable by agent, date range, repo, author, files touched.

Allows developers to build systems that react to events in our git repos (new commits, trail updates, gate results, etc.). Feeds into the automation platform.

Independent auth solution replacing GitHub as provider with SSO/SAML options. Enables group-level policies, configuration, and seat management.

Subscription and plan management on top of Stripe primitives: free tier, group tier, enterprise later. E.g. usage metering, payment processing, invoicing, upgrades/downgrades. Gate premium features. Don’t reinvent the wheel. We’re not going to compete on billing. It is not our core competency.

### **Repositories**

Git hosting to push, clone, browse, manage repos on our own infrastructure. The surface that replaces GitHub to power new functionality (below).

### **Trails**

Replace pull requests as the primary unit of agent-to-human collaboration. Branch-centric work containers with lifecycle tracking, threaded discussions, comment resolution, and linked checkpoints. Dependency for Gates.

### **Gates**

Quality and compliance evaluations that run automatically on trail commits. The flight deck showing current trail status, optimized for human consumption. Lets teams trust agent output at scale. Let us pre-evaluate OSS PRs. Depends on: Trails, Automation Platform.

### **Trail Runner**

Both a way to run agents easily (remote or local) and a way of managing workflows with which we could automate the handling of a trail. Or even build dark factory patterns.

The CLI is the programmatic interface allowing agents (and humans alike) interact with the entire platform: logging checkpoints, creating trails, triggering gates, reading context. Continue expanding agent coverage for new and emerging agents.

### **Activity**

Aggregated activity/contribution metrics at org, team, and user level as well as repo & groups of repos level. Parked until the capture gap card lands. This extends [ENT-3204](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-3204/agent-insights-trail-breakdown-read-tokens-per-session-tree-with-basis)'s breakdown tree below the session level, with node `kind`s `subagent`, `tool`, `skill`, `context`, `carry` and `other`.

Recommended shape, from the 2026-10-18 spike:

* **Exact nodes:** subagents.
* **Estimated nodes:** tools, scored as their output plus the input they add to later calls. Detect cache misses and charge them to carry, not to tools.
* **Skills:** load cost only. Their real cost is the cache reads their content draws later, about 19 to 68 times the load cost, which only shows through residency-based carry children (estimated). Keep "work under a skill" out of the summed tree.
* **Sums:** children sum to the parent for every token field. `calls` does not sum. Each node carries `basis`.

Needs new per-call extraction: subagent links, tool argument and result sizes, the components each call takes in, skill loads, and compaction. That should come through the shared `cli/transcript` library.

## Scope and method

Ran about 50 `librarian query` searches (unscoped, `--since 60d/30d/14d`) across the team, peregrine and agent-analytics/agent-insights.

Three limits on the evidence:
- **`--since 365d` returned HTTP 504 every time**, so "last 12 months" coverage comes from unscoped queries filtered by date, not a clean windowed search.
- **`--author` does not exist** on this librarian version.
- **Slack snippets are often only the first message**; three threads I'd most want (noted below) came back with no body.

Raw result JSON is in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-alex-workspace/d93a0699-2cb2-4509-87b3-5334b60e7b79/scratchpad/sl/`.

## Step 1: org context

`librarian admin config get org-context` says **nothing about a Semantic Layer team**: no charter, members, channel or Linear key.

- The roster is dated 2026-04-22 and is stale. It lists Evis Drenova as "Peregrine (semantic search)", Alisha Kawaguchi as "entire.io (Checkpoints analysis, Dispatches), CLI E2E", and Alex Ong as "Entire-Core (auth), Fleet".
- People active in the area but missing from the roster: Suhaan, Karthik Rameshkumar, hidde, Russell, jdx, Abhi Singh, Joseph, Lizzie, Haimantika.
- Linear teams listed: Entire (ENT), Core (COR), Troy, entire-cli OSS, DevRel. There is no semantic-layer team key. Search, peregrine and agent-insights work is filed under ENT; brain under COR.
- It notes "Team membership is fluid" and a DRI model with no PMs.

---

## A. The Semantic Layer team

**I found no charter, ownership statement or member list.** Everything below is pieced together from channel activity; membership is my inference.

### Origins of the term
- **linear_issue, 2025-11-20, ENT-7 "Do we want / can store Actions / Checklist in the semantic layer"** (Backlog). Earliest use of the term found. https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-7/do-we-want-can-store-actions-checklist-in-the-semantic-layer
- **github_content, 2026-03-31, `entirehq/company-knowledge/handbook/company/strategy.md` ("Entire Strategy: Now ⇢ July 2026")**. The only strategy-level statement: the Automation Platform "together with Trails and Checkpoints, [is] the first step toward the Semantic Reasoning Layer". It also lists "Search: full-text search across transcripts, prompts, and tool call content" under Foundation. The doc's horizon ended July 2026; I found no successor.
- **github_pr, 2026-04-21, entirehq/librarian#29 "docs: three-layer architecture + Entire semantic-layer reframe"** (Alex). Frames Librarian as "Entire's Semantic Reasoning Layer" with retrieval → graph → synthesis. https://github.com/entirehq/librarian/pull/29
- **linear_issue, 2026-04-21, ENT-513 "Spike: ingest Entire checkpoint data as a Librarian source"** (Backlog). https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-513/spike-ingest-entire-checkpoint-data-as-a-librarian-source
- **slack_thread, 2026-04-21**. ashtom: "both Marvin and Librarian should be Entire features… the tech itself, we should make available to everyone". https://slack.com/archives/C09CQJX69QB/p1776753274207099?thread_ts=1776753274.207099&cid=C09CQJX69QB

## B. Peregrine (code search)

**What it is:** a Rust code-search service over a trigram index, written to `.pg` index files in per-region S3 buckets. It runs as separate index and query tiers on EKS and is reached only through the entire-api gateway, with per-user authz via SpiceDB. It serves code search and symbols on the web and in the CLI. It is separate from `entire-search`, the semantic search over transcripts and commits (Georg, 2026-06-01: "entire-search is separate from peregrine").

**Who:** Evis Drenova authored nearly everything. Alisha Kawaguchi did region promotes and monitors. dvydra, nodo and paul appear on the ops side.

## C. agent-analytics / agent-insights

**Naming:** the service, repo and Linear cards are all `agent-insights` (`et/entirehq/agent-insights`). "agent-analytics" appears only in two of Alex's #progress posts (2026-10-15 and 10-19) describing the same thing, and Cole calls it "session analytics". I treat them as one product; that is inference from context, not a stated rename.

**What it is:** a service that reads checkpoint transcripts from EntireDB and trail data from entire-api, computes per-Trail token "TCO" by model and by activity, and serves a read API fronted by entire-api under `/insights`. It is registered as a core plugin with opt-in install. It surfaces as an "Agent insights" section on repo Analytics and a token activity strip on Trails.

**Who:** Alex Ong is DRI and main author. Alisha Kawaguchi did the deployment split, NATS consumers, dashboards and flag removal. Design input came from dipree and Jakub.

## B. Peregrine (code search)

**What it is:** a Rust code-search service over a trigram index, written to `.pg` index files in per-region S3 buckets. It runs as separate index and query tiers on EKS and is reached only through the entire-api gateway, with per-user authz via SpiceDB. It serves code search and symbols on the web and in the CLI. It is separate from `entire-search`, the semantic search over transcripts and commits (Georg, 2026-06-01: "entire-search is separate from peregrine").

**Who:** Evis Drenova authored nearly everything. Alisha Kawaguchi did region promotes and monitors. dvydra, nodo and paul appear on the ops side.

"agent-analytics" appears only in two of Alex's #progress posts (2026-10-15 and 10-19) describing the same thing, and Cole calls it "session analytics".
